Detection Thresholds — Defaults, Rationale, and When to Change

Source: THRESHOLDS.md

Flag thresholds are scientific judgments, not just config values. Defaults are deliberately lenient — appropriate for a general healthy-adult sample where the goal is to catch data-entry errors and gross outliers, not to diagnose insomnia. For clinical samples (insomnia, elderly, shift-work), revisit every row.

Provenance: defaults tuned on healthy young-adult university EMA sample. Document your own study population here so downstream users know the reference.

How to use these values

  • For our study data the values below are fixed. They are the rules the study ran with. The Step 5 limits (7, 7 and 24 hours for errors; 3, 15, 3 and 3 hours for unusual records) were written down in the project’s March 2026 logic document. The code has used these same values since the first release (July 2026) until they became configuration (see NEWS.md). To reproduce our results, keep the defaults.
  • For your own data you decide. Every key in the table can be set in your config YAML (the commented examples are in inst/config_template.yaml). The pipeline applies what you set and reports it; it does not choose rules for you. A value that is present but not a number stops the run.
  • Every run states the rules it used. The run prints === Rules in effect for this run === and saves the same list as output/effective_rules.csv (key, value, default, whether the value comes from the default or from your config, meaning). Keep that file with your results and cite it in your Methods. To compare two runs, compare their effective_rules.csv.

Threshold table

Config key Default Flags Rationale
classification.metric_validation.sol.excessive_minutes 120 SOL > 2h Very lenient. Clinical SOL marker ~30 min (Lichstein et al.). 2h catches only gross outliers.
classification.metric_validation.se.min_valid_percent 0 SE < 0% Structural impossibility → always flag
classification.metric_validation.se.max_valid_percent 100 SE > 100% Structural impossibility → always flag
classification.flag_severity.poor_efficiency_threshold_pct 70 SE < 70% Lenient. Insomnia cutoff ~85%. 70% flags markedly poor efficiency.
classification.flag_severity.high_sol_threshold_hours 1 SOL > 1h Lenient vs 30-min clinical marker.
classification.flag_severity.high_waso_threshold_hours 1.5 WASO > 1.5h Lenient. Clinical WASO marker often > 30 min.
classification.metric_validation.tst_tib_ratio.min_ratio 0.5 TST/TIB < 0.5 Equivalent to SE < 50%
classification.metric_validation.tst_tib_ratio.max_ratio 1.0 TST/TIB > 1.0 Impossible → hard error
timestamp.sequence.max_gap_hours 12 AM/PM flip trigger Assumes no legitimate interval >= 12h
timestamp.midnight_threshold_hour 6 Times < 6AM → next day Standard diary convention
classification.step5.error.bed_to_sleep_max_hours 7 |sleep − bed| > 7 h is an error Nobody takes 7 hours to fall asleep; more likely one of the two times was mis-entered
classification.step5.error.awake_to_getup_max_hours 7 |getup − awake| > 7 h is an error Lying in bed more than 7 h after waking is implausible
classification.step5.error.sleep_to_awake_max_hours 24 |awake − sleep| > 24 h is an error A sleep period cannot exceed a day
classification.step5.unusual.sleep_to_awake_min_hours / _max_hours 3 / 15 Sleep period < 3 h or > 15 h is unusual Possible but worth a look
classification.step5.unusual.bed_to_sleep_max_hours 3 Sleep − bed > 3 h is unusual Most people fall asleep within an hour
classification.step5.unusual.awake_to_getup_max_hours 3 Getup − awake > 3 h is unusual Long time in bed after waking
review.clean_categories clean, equal_time_ok, reasonable_unusual Final categories that count as “now passes” in the review status table Yours to define
manual_corrections.manual_overrides_parser false true: a manual sleep-metric-duration row wins over the interval parser Long-standing behaviour is that the parser wins; every skipped row is listed in output/manual_corrections_not_applied.csv
timestamp.interval.mmss_threshold_minutes 60 value > 60 with : → MM:SS Heuristic for ambiguous formats

Suggested config comments

Add rationale inline next to each threshold:

  flag_severity:
    poor_efficiency_threshold_pct: 70   # lenient (healthy sample). Clinical cutoff ~85%
    high_sol_threshold_hours: 1         # lenient. Clinical marker ~30 min
    high_waso_threshold_hours: 1.5      # lenient. Clinical marker ~30 min
  metric_validation:
    sol:
      excessive_minutes: 120            # gross-outlier catch, not clinical

What the validation shows about these defaults (and what it does not)

These values are reference values, not optimized ones. The synthetic benchmark swept the adjacent-swap threshold (1 to 5 h) and the AM/PM flip threshold (8 to 14 h) over a 20-point grid: recall stayed between 0.9950 and 0.9957 and false alarms stayed at zero. The benchmark is therefore insensitive to these two thresholds over that range; it cannot tell 3 h from 2 h or 4 h, and it does not show that 3 h and 12 h are optimal. On the study data no threshold changed the mean total sleep time by more than 0.93 minutes or the number of analysable rows by more than 0.70%. The defaults were set on a healthy young-adult sample and should be re-checked on your own data (validation/synthetic/operating_point_sweep.R is the template).

References

  • Lichstein et al. (2003), Behaviour Research and Therapy — quantitative criteria for insomnia (30-min SOL/WASO, ~85% SE)
  • AASM standard actigraphy-diary reporting conventions
